The regional standard specifies 6 sqm of net useful area per child across designated activity, rest, and toilet functions; this is not a whole-property gross-area threshold, and the available data do not establish whether those spaces are provided. Urban-planning compatibility, the host school's requirements, authorization, layout, accessibility, health and safety compliance, and the applicable regulatory framework at the application date all require verification. Strong proximity indicators and an A1 energy class add appeal, though the recorded plant and renewables scores are low.
pros: Existing school and educational use, consistent with the requirement for a spring section integrated with a kindergarten, subject to confirmation that the host facility meets applicable requirements.
Recorded gross area of 7,080.07 sqm exceeds the requested 180 sqm; capacity for 14 children is within the supplied verified regional range of 6–20.
Recent construction (2020), A1 energy class, and strong reported proximity percentiles across healthcare, mobility, green space, sport, commerce, and education.
cons: The data do not confirm that the required dedicated net areas—6 sqm per child across activity, rest, and toilet functions—are available or suitably laid out.
Turin PRG compatibility, building title and any change of use, sector authorization, accessibility, hygiene, and applicable fire and structural safety requirements remain to be checked.
Despite the A1 class, the recorded thermal plant and renewables sub-scores are low, and the overall energy sub-score total is 10.

evaluation_results.evaluation_text: This 535.56 sqm property is identified as a school and educational building, constructed in 2020, making it a strong strategic candidate for a spring section integrated with an existing kindergarten in Turin. Its gross area exceeds the requested 180 sqm, and the requested capacity of 14 falls within the stated regional range of 6–20 children. The verified regional standard is 6 sqm per child of net usable space across designated areas for ordinary activities, rest/free activities, and toilets; this is a functional-area requirement, not a minimum gross area for the whole property. The supplied data do not establish the availability or layout of those rooms, authorization, or planning and technical compliance. Verify the requirements applicable at the application date, including host-facility conditions, Turin planning compatibility, change of use or building title, hygiene, accessibility, fire safety where required, structural safety, and the sector authorization process. The location has high reported proximity percentiles across healthcare, mobility, green space, sports, commercial services, and education. Energy class A1 and the excellent envelope score are strengths, while the thermal plant and renewables scores are low. The deterministic relevance score is retained as provided.
pros: Existing school and educational use aligns with the objective of integrating a spring section into a kindergarten; the building dates from 2020.
Reported gross area of 535.56 sqm is above the requested 180 sqm, and capacity of 14 is within the stated 6–20-child range.
Strong reported local accessibility and services, with all six proximity percentiles between 90 and 93.38; energy class A1 and envelope score 5 are favorable.
cons: The property data do not confirm suitable net usable areas, room layout, toilets, or rest and activity spaces for the 14 children.

Planning compatibility, host-facility requirements, authorization, and building, hygiene, accessibility, fire, and structural compliance require verification; the applicable regulatory transition also needs checking.
Thermal plant and renewable-energy scores are both 1, which temper the otherwise favorable energy profile.
